Tests of suggested fixes for "undeclared name" diagnostics,
which are of ("compiler", "error") type.

-- flags --
-ignore_extra_diags

-- go.mod --
module example.com
go 1.12

-- a.go --
package undeclared_var

func a() {
	z, _ := 1+y, 11 //@quickfix("y", re"(undeclared name|undefined): y", a)
	_ = z
}

-- funclit.go --
package undeclared_var

// The undeclared name is used in a function literal that is not
// within a function declaration.

var _ = func(args []string) {
	verbose = len(args) > 0 //@quickfix("verbose", re"(undeclared name|undefined): verbose", funclit)
	println(verbose)
}

var _ = func() int {
	return count + 1 //@quickfix("count", re"(undeclared name|undefined): count", funclit_first)
}

// The undefined ident is assigned in a sibling function literal, which
// is a different scope: declaring it there would not fix the error at
// the cursor.

func siblingScope() {
	g1 := func() {
		x = "hello"
	}
	g2 := func() {
		var y int = x //@quickfix("x", re"(undeclared name|undefined): x", closure)
		_ = y
	}
	_, _ = g1, g2
}

// The assignment in the outer block dominates the use in the inner
// one, so it gets the missing colon.

func outerBlock(cond bool) {
	x = 1
	if cond {
		println(x) //@quickfix("x", re"(undeclared name|undefined): x", outer_block)
	}
}

+	verbose := len(args) > 0 //@quickfix("verbose", re"(undeclared name|undefined): verbose", funclit)
-- @funclit_first/funclit.go --
